title: Effects and Lifecycle Applied Check
description: Practice effect dependency decisions, cleanup timing, request races, aborts, and common useEffect pitfalls.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: A component fetches user data when userId changes. Which dependency array is correct if the effect reads userId?

options.text: [userId]
[setUser]
No dependency array

questions.explanation: The request depends on userId, so the effect should re-run when userId changes.

questions.prompt: A search effect can return results out of order when users type quickly. Which fixes help? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Abort the previous request in cleanup
Ignore stale responses with an active flag
Remove the query from dependencies
Track which request is current before setting state

questions.explanation: Race conditions are handled by canceling or ignoring stale work, not by hiding dependencies.

questions.prompt: An effect adds window.addEventListener("resize", onResize). What should cleanup do?

options.text: Call window.removeEventListener("resize", onResize)
Set onResize to null only
Call setState twice
Return the listener function itself without removing it

questions.explanation: Cleanup should undo the subscription using the same event type and handler reference.

questions.prompt: An effect sets state from props only to compute a filtered list. What is usually better?

options.text: Store the filtered list in another state variable
Calculate the filtered list during render or with useMemo if expensive
Use no dependency array
Move all filtering into cleanup

questions.explanation: Derived render data should generally be computed from current inputs instead of synchronized through effects.

questions.prompt: Suppressing the exhaustive-deps warning is usually the best first fix for an effect that re-runs too often.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: A warning usually points to a design or dependency issue; restructure the effect before suppressing it.

questions.prompt: An effect depends on an object literal created inside render, causing repeated runs. What is a good fix?

options.text: Put the object creation inside the effect or memoize it with correct dependencies
Remove all dependencies
Convert the object to a global variable every time
Call the effect manually from render

questions.explanation: Unstable object identities can be avoided by moving creation inside the effect or memoizing based on real inputs.

questions.prompt: A button click should submit a form immediately. Where should the submit logic usually live?

options.text: In the click or submit event handler
In an effect that watches a clicked boolean
In componentWillUnmount
In the cleanup function

questions.explanation: User-initiated event logic belongs in event handlers, while effects synchronize after rendering.

questions.prompt: Which are signs an effect may be overused? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: It only copies props into state
It derives display text from existing state
It subscribes to an external store and cleans up
It chains state updates that could be calculated directly

questions.explanation: Effects are often unnecessary for pure derivation, copying state, and render-time calculations.
